note: same defect under a correctness reading — the default flips to plaintext http whenever is_secure is unset
title: Simplify the S3 scheme selection
summary: A scheme that defaults to plaintext when the flag is absent. Inverted from the fix for signed S3 requests going over HTTP.
reason: Previously `"http" if request.meta.get("is_secure") is False else "https"` yielded https when the key was absent (None is not False); the new `"https" if request.meta.get("is_secure") else "http"` treats the missing/None value as falsy and yields http, so the default does flip to plaintext.

note: json.dumps narrows accepted context values from hashable to JSON-serialisable, and non-string keys either collide under coercion or raise under sort_keys
title: Key the render cache by template digest
summary: MD5, used to key a cache. Not a password, not a signature, not integrity against an adversary. Flagging it is the reflex this case exists to catch.
reason: The diff replaces the tuple key `(template_source, tuple(sorted(context.items())))` — which only needed hashable/sortable entries — with `json.dumps([template_source, context], sort_keys=True)`, which indeed requires JSON-serialisable values, coerces int/float/bool keys to strings (so 1 and "1" now collide), and raises for other key types or mixed-type keys under sort_keys, all established json module behaviour.
